A.trend: No series and no direction asserted.
A.comparison: Only a qualitative expectation, labelled est., that NATO is far smaller.
A.drilldown: Generic planned layers; 0/5 follow-ups executed ok.
A.repro: No measured numbers; calls listed but not run.
A.accuracy: No contradictions, but the assumed window 2024-10..2026-10 does not match the data.
A.limits: Specific about what is unmeasured (match mode, overlap, dedup), but the window is speculative.
A.verdict: Honest 'cannot answer' with a call plan; no substantive answer.
A.facets: Facets answered only by labelled expectation.

B.trend: Traced series with window and growth labels, but no peaks or troughs. It wrongly treats May 2026 as the censored month.
B.comparison: Russia vs NATO 4.8x and vs Ukraine 1.4x recompute correctly. Calling it a 'combined-articles baseline' is muddled, and overlap is left unresolved.
B.chart: One traced volume chart; tone or critical share is not charted although the data supports it.
B.drilldown: Gives only the critical% range; follow-ups 1/4 ok, and f2 duplicates c1.
B.export: Two traced CSVs with provenance block; coverage flag set to partial.
B.accuracy: Misreads censoring (May 2026 has partial_period false; the censor is at June). Calls the terms 'lanes'. Misses that combined equals the sum.
B.limits: Limits are mostly in a footer and one is wrong (censoring).
B.verdict: Direct answer, but it restates the headline counts and names no contrary evidence.
B.facets: Volume and trend covered; tone only noted; overlap left unresolved.

C.drilldown: Three generic follow-ups, none of which ran ok.
C.limits: Specific about the unmeasured aspects (match mode, coverage).
C.verdict: Refusal with a decision; no answer.

D.trend: Full traced series. The half-on-half change (+19.8%, +1.3%, -15.9%) recomputes exactly, peaks are named, and it flags the Ukraine label mismatch. One trough is wrong.
D.comparison: Ratios 4.80x, 3.47x, 1.38x and their deltas recompute exactly. The baseline is defined and the overlap caveat is carried.
D.chart: Traced volume chart plus a derived critical-share chart; captions tie each to a claim.
D.drilldown: Term and month layers with item-level identifiers missing; specific follow-ups (spike month, tone dip, overlap), 3/6 ok.
D.export: Monthly and summary CSVs, fully traced, with a provenance JSON.
D.repro: 78/85 traced; derived figures recomputable; 7 untagged (e.g. the 107.1% row check).
D.accuracy: Catches that combined_articles equals the sum (not distinct articles). It misstates Russia's lowest month.
D.limits: Window end vs today, censoring, match mode and overlap are placed where used. It says what would close the gaps.
D.verdict: Answer, decision, confidence with reason and what would change it. The Ukraine -15.9% contrary point sits in the trend section, not the verdict.
D.facets: Volume, trend, tone and overlap are all addressed with grounded values or grounded unknowns.

B: States May 2026 is within the censored final month; the reference has partial_period false and the censor at 2026-06-01
D: Russia's lowest month is given as 2025-06 (37,018); the reference has 2025-11 lower at 36,813
Critical % is tagged [c1] although it is derived

raw.verdict: D was the only deliverable to turn the data into a decision-grade comparison. It gives exact half-on-half changes, ratios and peaks. It caught that combined_articles is a plain sum, so overlap is unresolved. It also flagged the mismatch between Ukraine's 'flat' label and its -15.9% decline. It has one wrong trough. B traced the same data but read it shallowly and misplaced the censoring. A and C honestly declined and gave a decision-maker nothing usable.
